financials_interim.notes: Company (standalone parent-entity) basis. Source: ACL Plastics PLC Interim Financial Statements for the period ended 30 June 2026 (unaudited, signed 13 Aug 2026), downloaded from CSE cdn. This is the FIRST financial_statements row entered for APLA in this DB, so only YoY (vs the filing's own comparative quarter ended 30 June 2025) is computed, no QoQ. APLA has a 31 March financial year end -> this is Q1 FY2026/27. Separate Group and Company columns given throughout -> entered as two rows (GROUP and COMPANY) per project convention. APLA is 65.21% owned by ACL Cables PLC (per the 20-largest-shareholders note, p.6) -- ACL's own Q1 FY2026/27 Group interim (already in this DB) showed consolidated 'Results from operating activities' FALLING 12.6% YoY (1,939,323 vs 2,220,195), so APLA's own 25.4% operating-profit growth this quarter is running counter to, and partially offsetting, the wider ACL group's operating trend. Income statement p.2, balance sheet p.3, cash flow p.4, equity note (shares/market data) p.6. Sign convention: cost_of_sales stored as positive magnitude; capex stored as positive magnitude; cash flow lines keep natural sign. 'Net finance (cost)/income' is disclosed as a SINGLE NET line (no separate gross finance income/cost split) -> stored in finance_income (Group 138,937 / Company 136,172), finance_costs left at 0, matching this project's ACL/RICH precedent for single-net-line filers. Group cost_of_sales (487,343) is LOWER than Company's (507,242) for identical revenue (738,546 both) -- Group gross profit (251,203) exceeds Company gross profit (231,303) by exactly the elimination of an intercompany cost markup; this is as printed, not an extraction artifact. short_term_borrowings = 'Bank overdraft' only (Group 92,769 / Company 93,211 at 30.06.2026; zero at 31.03.2026) -- this is the only interest-bearing line on either balance sheet. long_term_borrowings = 0 for both (no non-current interest-bearing debt disclosed). cash_and_equivalents (6,096 both) is the balance-sheet 'Cash and cash equivalents' line only; 'Short term investments' (974,222) and 'Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss' (1,692,363) are separate BS lines, excluded, since they are investment assets rather than cash equivalents. Shares in issue (42,125,000) per note 1 (Non-Financial Information, p.6); EPS reconciles exactly: Group 294,527/42,125,000=6.99, Company 279,339/42,125,000=6.63. Plastics resin / FX: the filing discloses an explicit exchange-gain note (Note 8, p.6): 'Exchange Gain/(Loss)' of Rs.85,395k this quarter vs Rs.12,771k a year earlier (>500% higher), embedded within the net finance line -- this is the single most identifiable driver of the net-finance-income surge, though the filing gives no separate commentary on plastics resin input costs (see gaps_note).

interim_updates.note_text: ACL Plastics PLC (APLA, 65.21%-owned by ACL Cables PLC) reported Group revenue of Rs.738.5mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), up 4.97% YoY from Rs.703.6mn, while gross profit jumped 47.0% to Rs.251.2mn (from Rs.197.9mn) as cost of sales fell 3.6% to Rs.487.3mn (from Rs.505.7mn) -- gross margin expanded roughly 9 percentage points, from 28.1% to 34.0%, consistent with a favourable plastics-resin input-cost or sales-mix shift (no explicit management commentary is given -- see gaps_note). Group operating profit rose 25.4% YoY to Rs.245.7mn (from Rs.196.0mn) even after administrative expenses nearly tripled to Rs.5.5mn (from Rs.1.9mn). Below the operating line, net finance income surged 178.9% YoY to Rs.138.9mn (from Rs.49.8mn), driven substantially by an exchange gain of Rs.85.4mn disclosed in Note 8 (versus Rs.12.8mn a year earlier, per the filing's own 'Exchange Gain/(Loss)' breakdown) plus an unrealised exchange gain on fixed-deposit investments of Rs.66.4mn (versus nil a year earlier) and an unrealised FVTPL gain of Rs.39.2mn (versus Rs.25.1mn, +56.4%) shown in the cash flow statement's reconciling items. Profit before tax rose 56.5% YoY to Rs.384.6mn (from Rs.245.8mn), tax expense rose 34.4% to Rs.90.1mn (from Rs.67.0mn), and profit after tax rose 64.8% to Rs.294.5mn (from Rs.178.8mn); basic EPS rose to Rs.6.99 from Rs.4.24. At Company level the swing was even larger -- PBT +48.9% to Rs.362.9mn, PAT +58.3% to Rs.279.3mn -- but Company cost of sales was essentially flat (Rs.507.2mn vs Rs.505.7mn), so all of the Company-level margin gain came from the smaller administrative-expense base and the finance-income surge rather than from the cost-of-sales improvement visible at Group level. Working capital absorbed cash this quarter: inventories rose Rs.197.5mn (per the cash flow statement) and trade & other receivables rose Rs.228.9mn, driving net cash used in Group operating activities to Rs.(194.8)mn from a small Rs.20.4mn inflow a year earlier.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for APLA in this database, so no prior quarter (e.g. Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column (quarter ended 30 June 2025) is used. Genuine disclosure gaps: (1) the filing contains no MD&A / directors' commentary section, so there is no explicit management text confirming plastics-resin input-cost trends as the cause of the gross-margin expansion -- this is inferred from the cost-of-sales and revenue lines only, and is flagged as an inference rather than a disclosed fact. (2) 'Net finance (cost)/income' is disclosed as a single net line with only partial sub-components broken out (Note 8's exchange gain, and the cash flow statement's unrealised FX/FVTPL reconciling items) -- there is no full bridge from the Rs.49.8mn prior-year net finance figure to the Rs.138.9mn current figure, so a residual (~Rs.14.8mn: 138,937 - 85,395 - 66,366 - 39,227 + underlying interest income of 14,917 and interest expense of 603, per the cash flow statement's own adjustments) could not be independently attributed to a named driver. (3) The Group vs Company cost-of-sales gap (487,343 vs 507,242, both against identical 738,546 revenue) is not explained by any note -- it is presented as-is and read as an intercompany-cost elimination on consolidation, but the filing does not state this explicitly.
interim_updates.takeaway: Group PAT rose 64.8% YoY (Rs.178.8mn to Rs.294.5mn) on two distinct legs: a genuine operating improvement (gross margin +9pp to 34.0% as cost of sales fell 3.6% against 5.0% revenue growth, lifting operating profit +25.4% to Rs.245.7mn) and a large non-operating tailwind below the line (net finance income +178.9% to Rs.138.9mn, mostly an Rs.85.4mn exchange gain per Note 8 plus a Rs.66.4mn unrealised FX gain on fixed deposits that did not recur from the prior year). APLA's own operating improvement is notable against its 65.21% parent ACL Cables PLC's Group interim, whose consolidated operating profit fell 12.6% YoY over the same quarter -- APLA is outperforming the wider ACL group. The main offsetting item is working capital: inventories and receivables both built up this quarter, pushing net operating cash flow to Rs.(194.8)mn from a positive Rs.20.4mn a year earlier.
operational_highlights: Group revenue up 4.97% YoY to Rs.738.5mn (from Rs.703.6mn); gross profit up 47.0% to Rs.251.2mn as cost of sales fell 3.6% to Rs.487.3mn -- gross margin expanded from 28.1% to 34.0%
Group operating profit up 25.4% YoY to Rs.245.7mn (from Rs.196.0mn) despite administrative expenses nearly tripling to Rs.5.5mn (from Rs.1.9mn)

Net finance income surged 178.9% YoY to Rs.138.9mn (from Rs.49.8mn) -- Note 8 discloses an embedded exchange gain of Rs.85.4mn this quarter vs Rs.12.8mn a year earlier; the cash flow statement also shows an unrealised exchange gain on fixed deposits of Rs.66.4mn (nil a year earlier) and an unrealised FVTPL gain of Rs.39.2mn (+56.4% from Rs.25.1mn)
Group PBT up 56.5% YoY to Rs.384.6mn (from Rs.245.8mn); PAT up 64.8% to Rs.294.5mn (from Rs.178.8mn); basic EPS Rs.6.99 (from Rs.4.24)

Company-level PBT rose faster in percentage terms (+48.9% to Rs.362.9mn) despite Company cost of sales being flat (Rs.507.2mn vs Rs.505.7mn) -- the Company-level gain came almost entirely from the finance-income surge and a smaller admin-expense base, not from a cost-of-sales improvement

Working capital absorbed cash: inventories +Rs.197.5mn and trade & other receivables +Rs.228.9mn this quarter (per the cash flow statement), driving net cash used in Group operating activities to Rs.(194.8)mn from a Rs.20.4mn inflow a year earlier

APLA (65.21% owned by ACL Cables PLC) grew Group operating profit 25.4% this quarter while ACL's own consolidated Group operating profit fell 12.6% YoY over the same quarter (per ACL's Q1 FY2026/27 interim, already in this DB) -- APLA is running counter to its parent group's operating trend
key_drivers: Gross margin expansion from 28.1% to 34.0% at Group level (cost of sales -3.6% YoY vs revenue +5.0%) -- the clearest operating-line driver, though the filing gives no explicit commentary on plastics resin input costs to confirm the cause (see gaps_note)
Exchange gain of Rs.85.4mn this quarter vs Rs.12.8mn a year earlier (Note 8, p.6, >500% higher) -- the single largest identifiable component of the 178.9% surge in net finance income to Rs.138.9mn

Unrealised exchange gain on investment in fixed deposits of Rs.66.4mn this quarter vs nil a year earlier, and unrealised gain on financial assets at FVTPL of Rs.39.2mn (+56.4% from Rs.25.1mn) -- both per the cash flow statement's reconciling items, together the rest of the net-finance-income surge

Working capital build (inventories +Rs.197.5mn, trade & other receivables +Rs.228.9mn) pushed net cash used in Group operating activities to Rs.(194.8)mn from a Rs.20.4mn inflow a year earlier -- the main item working against an otherwise strong quarter
